sentences.text: The Lincoln -- Douglas Debates -LRB- also known as The Great Debates of 1858 -RRB- were a series of seven debates between Abraham Lincoln , the Republican candidate for the United States Senate from Illinois , and incumbent Senator Stephen Douglas , the Democratic Party candidate .	Abraham Lincoln	Abraham Lincoln	Republican	Republican Party (United States)	United States Senate	United States Senate	Illinois	Illinois	Stephen Douglas	Stephen Douglas	Democratic Party	Democratic Party (United States)

At the time , U.S. senators were elected by state legislatures ; thus Lincoln and Douglas were trying for their respective parties to win control of the Illinois legislature .	Illinois	Illinois	state legislatures	state legislature (United States)
The debates previewed the issues that Lincoln would face in the aftermath of his victory in the 1860 presidential election .	1860 presidential election	United States presidential election, 1860

Although Illinois was a free state , the main issue discussed in all seven debates was slavery in the United States .	Illinois	Illinois	free state	slave and free states	slavery in the United States	slavery in the United States

In agreeing to the official debates , Lincoln and Douglas decided to hold one debate in each of the nine congressional districts in Illinois .	Illinois	Illinois	congressional districts in Illinois	Illinois's congressional districts

Because both had already spoken in two -- Springfield and Chicago -- within a day of each other , they decided that their `` joint appearances '' would be held only in the remaining seven districts .	Springfield	Springfield, Illinois	Chicago	Chicago
The debates were held in seven towns in the state of Illinois :	Illinois	Illinois
Ottawa on August 21	Ottawa	Ottawa, Illinois
Freeport on August 27	Freeport	Freeport, Illinois
Jonesboro on September 15	Jonesboro	Jonesboro, Illinois
Charleston on September 18	Charleston	Charleston, Illinois
Galesburg on October 7	Galesburg	Galesburg, Illinois
Quincy on October 13	Quincy	Quincy, Illinois
Alton on October 15	Alton	Alton, Illinois

The debates in Freeport , Quincy and Alton drew especially large numbers of people from neighboring states , as the issue of slavery was of monumental importance to citizens across the nation .	Freeport	Freeport, Illinois	Quincy	Quincy, Illinois	Alton	Alton, Illinois
Newspaper coverage of the debates was intense .

Major papers from Chicago sent stenographers to create complete texts of each debate , which newspapers across the United States reprinted in full , with some partisan edits .	Chicago	Chicago	stenographers	Court reporter

Newspapers that supported Douglas edited his speeches to remove any errors made by the stenographers and to correct grammatical errors , while they left Lincoln 's speeches in the rough form in which they had been transcribed .	stenographers	Court reporter
In the same way , pro-Lincoln papers edited Lincoln 's speeches , but left the Douglas texts as reported .
After losing the election for Senator in Illinois , Lincoln edited the texts of all the debates and had them published in a book .	Illinois	Illinois

The widespread coverage of the original debates and the subsequent popularity of the book led eventually to Lincoln 's nomination for President of the United States by the 1860 Republican National Convention in Chicago .	Republican	Republican Party (United States)	Chicago	Chicago	President of the United States	President of the United States	1860 Republican National Convention	1860 Republican National Convention
The format for each debate was : one candidate spoke for 60 minutes , then the other candidate spoke for 90 minutes , and then the first candidate was allowed a 30-minute `` rejoinder . ''
The candidates alternated speaking first .
As the incumbent , Douglas spoke first in four of the debates .
